value: Grown throughout the hills for still white wine, with fruit from the cooler sites also used for sparkling wine.
source_notes: WA: a decent amount, especially from cooler sites, goes to sparkling | Halliday: grows throughout the Adelaide Hills; a significant proportion grown for sparkling

value: Medium weight and complex, held together by fresh natural acidity from the cool hills.
source_notes: WA: complex medium weight wines with good natural acidity | Halliday: natural acidity allows complex styles

value: South Australia's most highly regarded region for Pinot Noir, made as a still red and also as a base for sparkling wine.
source_notes: WA: leading SA region for high quality Pinot Noir; a proportion goes to sparkling | Halliday: regarded as the finest SA producer of pinot noir; significant proportion for sparkling

value: Usually medium bodied with soft tannins, ranging from earthy and spiced to fleshy and fruit forward depending on the site.
source_notes: WA: typically medium bodied, soft tannins | Halliday: styles from earthy, herbaceous and spiced to fruit forward and fleshy

value: One of the region's signature whites and widely seen as a benchmark for Australian Sauvignon Blanc.
source_notes: WA: often referred to as the benchmark for Australian Sauvignon Blanc | Halliday: best known variety; quotes Halliday 'one of Australia's best'

value: Leans towards ripe tropical fruit with only a hint of the green, herbal side, kept fresh by cold nights.
source_notes: WA: ripe tropical flavours with hints of gooseberry and herbaceousness | Halliday: cool climate and night chill yield tropical aromas

value: Grown alongside the region's Shiraz, it does best on the valley's cooler sites and in cooler years.
source_notes: WA: does best in cooler sites and cooler vintages | Halliday: performs best on cooler sites and in moderately cool vintages

value: Rich and ripe, with dense dark fruit and riper tannins than Cabernet from cooler regions.
source_notes: WA: richer with riper fruit and softer tannins | Halliday: rich black fruit; Jeroboams (merchant) also notes ripe tannins

value: Used in blends with Shiraz and Mataro, and also bottled on its own.
source_notes: WA: often blended with Shiraz and Mataro (GSM), also single varietal | Halliday: varietal wines and blends | Wine Folly: GSM blend of Grenache, Shiraz and Mataro

value: Ripe and juicy, with a sweet fruited richness and a touch of peppery spice.
source_notes: WA: rich with ripe raspberry and peppery spice | Halliday: juicily sweet, rich tapestry of flavours

value: Mostly used with Grenache and Shiraz in the region's GSM blends.
source_notes: WA: Grenache often blended with Shiraz and Mataro (GSM) | Wine Folly: a GSM blend contains Grenache, Shiraz and Mataro

value: Full bodied and plush, with soft ripe tannins and a velvety, mouth filling weight.
source_notes: WA: typically full bodied with ripe fruit and plush tannins | Halliday: lush, velvety and mouth filling, tannins ripe and soft

value: One of the two grapes the region's producers focus on, alongside Shiraz, grown on high altitude sites.
source_notes: WA: Chardonnay, Shiraz and Pinot Noir do very well in this altitude influenced area | Halliday: producers focus almost solely on chardonnay and shiraz

value: One of the two grapes the region's producers focus on, alongside Chardonnay.
source_notes: WA: Shiraz does very well in this altitude influenced area | Halliday: producers focus almost solely on chardonnay and shiraz

value: One of the district's leading whites, well suited to its cool climate.
source_notes: WA: arguably the most important and admired white variety | Halliday: among the star performers, well suited to cooler temperatures

value: One of the region's main red grapes, alongside Shiraz.
source_notes: WA: main varieties are Riesling, Shiraz and Cabernet Sauvignon | Halliday: drinkable reds from cabernet sauvignon and shiraz

value: Dark fruited and fleshy, with tannins that are firm but plush.
source_notes: WA: dark, rich black fruit with firm but plush tannins | Halliday: fleshy dark fruit, fine tannin, plush style

value: Tight and austere when young, it softens with bottle age into honeyed, toasty flavours.
source_notes: WA: restrained and austere when young, benefits from bottle age | Halliday: evolves from tart citrus to honey and toast

value: One of the region's main grapes, alongside Riesling and Cabernet Sauvignon.
source_notes: WA: main varieties are Riesling, Shiraz and Cabernet Sauvignon | Halliday: substantial riesling plantings nearly on par with shiraz; cabernet and shiraz reds

value: Medium to full bodied with ripe, juicy berry fruit and a balanced richness.
source_notes: WA: full flavoured with ripe blackberry, spice and mint | Halliday: juicy plum and berry fruit; medium to full bodied with balance and richness

value: A fairly recent arrival, used as a blending partner for Cabernet Sauvignon and also bottled on its own.
source_notes: WA: no long tradition; successful blending partner for Cabernet; elegant varietal wine | Halliday: fairly recent arrival, varietal and blending component

value: The region's original grape, now often blended with Cabernet Sauvignon in a local tradition.
source_notes: WA: main variety until the 1950s; Coonawarra tradition is to blend Shiraz and Cabernet | Halliday: until the 1950s the only grape; greatest reds are shiraz cabernet blends

value: A well regarded red here, grown alongside the region's Shiraz.
source_notes: WA: Cabernet around Eden Valley village is of the highest quality | Halliday: increasingly proving its red credentials with rich cabernet; does well

value: Pristine, lean and driven by fresh acidity.
source_notes: Halliday: pristine riesling | Wine Folly: a lean, acid driven style of dry Riesling

value: The region's leading red grape and home to some renowned vineyards.
source_notes: WA: most important red grape, often most highly regarded wine | Halliday: home to renowned Shiraz vineyards

value: Plush and smooth, with ripe, well integrated tannins.
source_notes: WA: very smooth with ripe, integrated tannins, luscious fruit | Halliday: plush shiraz

value: Grown across the region and one of its most acclaimed reds.
source_notes: WA: thrives across the region; vies with Riesling as most important wine | Halliday: acclaimed varietal from Mount Barker

value: Intense yet never heavy, tightly built and able to age well.
source_notes: WA: elegant, tightly structured, ages well | Halliday: intense without being too heavy; does well when aged

value: One of the region's leading wines, made in a crisp style.
source_notes: WA: vies with Cabernet as most important wine; crisp and lean in youth | Halliday: one of the favourite varietals, acclaimed for crisp flavour

value: Cool grown and spicy, with dark plum fruit and good texture.
source_notes: WA: liquorice, spice, pepper, black cherry and plum | Halliday: cool grown style, spicy blackberry and plum fruit, good texture

value: Once the mainstay of the region and still widely grown, though Shiraz is now its standout grape.
source_notes: WA: Cabernet is among the main varieties | Halliday: cabernet was the mainstay and still has a stronghold in plantings; shiraz is the standout star

value: Rich and generous, sometimes with a eucalyptus mint note typical of central Victoria.
source_notes: WA: rich and generous, classic central Victorian eucalypt mint in some vintages | Halliday: rich fruit; the south shows mint and spice

value: The main white grape in this mostly red region.
source_notes: WA: main varieties Shiraz, Chardonnay, Cabernet, Grenache (only white listed) | Halliday: Heathcote is shiraz country; great whites include fine chardonnay

value: A red on the rise, now counted among the region's main grapes.
source_notes: WA: Grenache among main varieties | Halliday: grenache among varieties on the rise

value: The region's standout grape and the one Heathcote is best known for.
source_notes: WA: produces world class Shiraz with a unique character | Halliday: Heathcote is shiraz country; shiraz is the standout star

value: Perfumed and medium to full bodied, with ripe fruit that is seldom green.
source_notes: WA: medium to full bodied, ripe cassis and violet aromas | Halliday: seldom green, juicy mid palate | MRWA: medium bodied, very perfumed and elegant

value: Crisp and juicy, with extra flesh on the middle palate from the maritime climate.
source_notes: WA: crisp, lively and juicy (said of the Sauvignon Blanc Semillon blends) | Halliday: maritime influence gives sauvignon blanc extra mid palate flesh

value: A long standing red here that takes a back seat to Cabernet Sauvignon.
source_notes: Margaret River Wine Association: Shiraz dates back to the earliest days, second red after Cabernet | Wine Folly Margaret River guide: Shiraz takes a back seat to Cabernet Sauvignon

value: Full bodied and opulent, with ripe, soft tannins.
source_notes: WA: full bodied with ripe, soft tannins | Halliday: easy drinking opulence

value: Leans to stone fruit and peach flavours, often with a toasty touch of oak.
source_notes: WA: fuller styles with peach and melon and varied oak | Halliday: toasty, stone fruited style

value: Perfumed and juicy, with spice and real complexity.
source_notes: WA: lively, juicy, raspberry scented and spicy | Halliday: perfumed, red fruited complexity

value: The region's dominant red grape.
source_notes: WA: Shiraz is still considered king | Halliday: shiraz dominates the landscape; a leading shiraz region

value: Elegant and citrus fresh, in styles ranging from lean to rich and creamy.
source_notes: WA: melon, citrus and fig | Halliday: elegance unites them; lean and citrusy to rich and creamy

value: A leading white of the peninsula, whose cool climate suits it ideally.
source_notes: WA: the cool climate is ideal for this variety | Halliday: pinot gris/grigio another champion; climate ideal for it

value: The peninsula's leading grape.
source_notes: WA: the most planted variety in the region | Halliday: the undisputed hero of the Mornington Peninsula

value: Light to medium bodied and delicate, ranging from bright and pretty to savoury and structured by site.
source_notes: WA: light to medium bodied, delicate, soft tannins | Halliday: delicate, from structured and savoury to pretty and bright

value: Often bottled on its own and sometimes blended with Merlot or Shiraz.
source_notes: Wine Australia (australianwine.com): sometimes blended with Merlot and Shiraz | Halliday: single variety wines common, sometimes blended with merlot, shiraz

value: Generous and luscious, with ripe berry fruit that balances the grape's natural tannin.
source_notes: Wine Australia: generous berry and dark chocolate flavours | Halliday: luscious fruit balances natural tannin

value: Full flavoured with stone fruit, and it improves with a few years in bottle.
source_notes: Wine Australia: full flavoured, ages well | Halliday: stone fruited, looks especially good after a few years

value: A blending partner for Cabernet Sauvignon in this mainly red region.
source_notes: Wine Australia: Cabernet sometimes blended with Merlot | Halliday: predominately red wine country incl. merlot; cabernet blended with merlot

value: A flagship red here, made in styles from elegant to robust.
source_notes: Wine Australia: flagship variety, elegant and bright to full flavoured and robust | Halliday: styles from structured savoury to easy drinking

value: The region's leading white, grown successfully at every elevation.
source_notes: WA: very important, grows well at all elevations | Halliday: foremost white, performs well across elevations

value: Thrives in the region's cool climate.
source_notes: WA: grows well in Orange's cool climate | Halliday: conditions see sauvignon blanc thrive

value: Aromatic and strongly tropical in flavour.
source_notes: WA: aromatic with strong tropical fruit | Halliday: signature tropical style

value: Full bodied and ripe, with firm tannins kept in balance by the fruit, and able to age.
source_notes: WA: ripe, spicy, great balance and age worthiness | Winemakers of Rutherglen: full bodied, firm high tannin, balance of fruit and tannin

value: Lighter and finer than Rutherglen Muscat, with candied fruit and caramel notes in place of its grapey richness.
source_notes: Winemakers of Rutherglen: lighter and finer than Muscat; candied fruit, honey, toffee | Rose Murray Brown (wine writer): more citric candied fruit than grapey Muscat, more caramelised notes

value: Very sweet, rich and intense, growing deeper and more complex with each step up the age classification.
source_notes: Winemakers of Rutherglen: very sweet, intense, rich | Halliday (Jeni Port): classification is a progression of richness, complexity, age and intensity

value: One of the region's key red grapes, alongside Durif.
source_notes: WA: main varieties Shiraz, Durif, Cabernet | Halliday: key varieties durif, shiraz, muscat, topaque

value: Rich, full bodied and powerful, with ripe fruit kept in balance.
source_notes: WA: full flavoured, rich, ripe fruit, supple tannins | Winemakers of Rutherglen: rich, full bodied, well balanced, powerful

value: Crisp, with a bright, lively acidity.
source_notes: WA: crisp Pinot Gris | Halliday: weight, spice, aromatics and acidity

value: Often blended with small amounts of Cabernet Franc and Merlot.
source_notes: WA: often blended with small proportions of Cabernet Franc and Merlot | Halliday: blending produces a range of styles

value: Ranges from medium to full bodied, often elegant and floral, with silky tannins.
source_notes: WA: medium to full bodied, silky tannins, perfumed and flowery | Halliday: full bodied to floral and aromatic; elegant

value: Shows white peach, melon and fig flavours.
source_notes: WA: white peach, melon and fig | Halliday: melon, fig and white peach

value: One of the valley's leading red grapes.
source_notes: WA: one of the premier red varieties | Halliday: the star of Yarra Valley red varieties

value: A rising red best suited to the valley's lower, warmer sites.
source_notes: WA: a rising star, site selection important | Halliday: lower, warmer sites best suited to shiraz
